What goes on that page:
5 principles. 

1. See Possibility Before Proof: We look for curiosity, trajectory, and capacity to grow, not just polished achievement.
2. Turn Ideas Into Action: Ideas only matter when they survive questioning, building, testing, and real-world use.
3. Raise Standards, Build More Ladders: We keep expectations high and reinforce support so hard growth can actually happen.
4. Own What Happens Next: We do not blame conditions. We choose the next meaningful action.
5. Let Truth Revise Us: We treat beliefs as hypotheses and update quickly when evidence changes.
Visual treatment: Bento grid, one principle per cell.
Image/Graphic Direction: Minimal icons or small symbolic illustrations per principle; no human photo.

What goes on that page:
Four archetypes:

- Product & Software Engineers: 
Engineers building products, systems, and software with a strong bias toward shipping.
- STEM Builders:
Students or graduates in science, mathematics, and applied technical fields who want to build real things.
- Final-Year Engineering Students:
Students in their last year of engineering who are ready to move from classroom learning to serious building.
- Ambitious Technical Founders:
Builders from adjacent or non-traditional backgrounds who are serious about creating technical companies.

What goes on that page:
Title: Weekly Missions.
Subhead: High-Velocity Execution & Feedback
Body: “Each week is built around a single Venture Mission, not an academic topic. The work begins before the theory, so the lesson arrives only after the problem is real.”

What goes on that page:
Title: Visible Progress. 
Subhead: The first draft comes first. Then the lecture. Then the revision.
Body: “Founders print the rough version before they are ready. After critique and teaching, they rebuild it. The difference between Version 1 and Version 2 is the proof that learning happened.”
Visual treatment: Split-screen or diptych layout: left = raw draft, right = refined draft.
Image/Graphic Direction: Before/after visual: sketch vs polished UI, messy notes vs clean framework, rough proposal vs improved version. This page should make improvement feel tangible.
